findings.claim: I1 holds only within one call: dedupe keeps no state, so redelivering an id in a later call creates a duplicate in history
evidence: dedupe.py:2 seen = set() is a local, recreated on every call
probe: h += dedupe([e]); h += dedupe([e]) -> id 1 appears twice
findings.failure_mechanism: id redelivered in a separate call -> the fresh seen set returns it again -> a caller that appends each output to history records it twice
findings.severity_change_reason: The contract fixes the interface as the stateless dedupe(events) and defines no history store; the duplicate needs a hypothetical caller that concatenates outputs from separate calls without deduping, and no such caller exists. Redelivered ids merged into the events passed to dedupe are removed: dedupe(history + retries) gave ids [1,2,3], and dedupe is idempotent.
findings.rejection_reason: The failure mechanism does not follow from the target: it depends on a caller outside the contract, and cross-call memory would be hidden global state the contract does not ask for. Merged with invariants-1.

findings.claim: An event id redelivered in a later call (a retry) is returned again because dedupe keeps no state between calls
findings.failure_mechanism: retry in a separate batch -> new empty seen set -> duplicate id in history built from the concatenated outputs
findings.severity_change_reason: Same root cause as acceptance-1; rejected for the same reason.
findings.rejection_reason: Duplicate of acceptance-1. The mechanism depends on concatenating outputs outside the function's contract; no history or caller in the target does this.

findings.claim: No test asserts which occurrence is kept, so a keep-last mutant passes all tests
evidence: test_dedupe.py:14-15 asserts only len and ids
findings.failure_mechanism: a future keep-last implementation -> tests stay green -> the later payload is retained
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: dedupe.py:5-7 keeps the first occurrence, confirmed by lead and reviewer probes. acceptance-2 and invariants-2 merged here.

findings.claim: No test shows the first-seen event is the one kept

findings.claim: All test inputs have ascending ids, so a sort-by-id mutant passes and first-seen order is not told apart from sorted order
findings.failure_mechanism: a sorting implementation -> tests pass -> [3,1,3] returned as [1,3]
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: the lead probe on ids [3,1,3,2] returned [3,1,2], so first-seen order holds.

findings.claim: No test delivers an id 3 or more times or across calls, so a toggle mutant that re-admits the id on its third delivery passes
findings.failure_mechanism: third delivery -> mutant re-appends it -> duplicate, tests stay green
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: the lead probe with id 1 delivered three times returned a single id-1 entry. The cross-call part is rejected under acceptance-1.
